items.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013
items.q: he had been a professional musician in England and he’d recorded all of Rudy Wiedoeft’s material on baritone.

ctx.x: Yes. It’s not bad to go down. Wow.

Yeah. Some guy in New Zealand showed me how to slap tongue. His name was Max Stewart, and he was a baritone player from England, who’d come to New Zealand and started a jewelry store. And he had been a professional musician in England and he’d recorded all of Rudy Wiedoeft’s material on baritone. So he did “Oodles of Noodles” and “Saxophobia,” and all those old corny things. And he showed me how to do this slap tongue thing. And it’s not about hitting here, it’s about hitting back. Like right off the © Hamilton…

roof of your mouth, so, and you have the reed in there. So you’re shutting the reed, and then the pressure behind it as you open the reed pops it. And you have just enough power to go through it to make the reed vibrate.
